scenario_source.notes: Degenerate case — both vehicles at 0 m/s. Exercises response-phase acceleration term only. Matches ad-rss-lib PhysicsUnitTestsStoppingDistance golden case at zero velocity under canonical test parameters.

description: ad-rss-lib constants (ρ=1, a_max_accel=3.5, a_min_rear=4, a_max_front=8). 0 + 0.5·3.5·1² + 3.5²/8 − 0 = 1.75 + 1.53125 = 3.28125 m.

scenario_source.notes: Ego ~54 km/h approaching stationary target. Typical CCRs-style test at mid-urban speed.
High-speed approach to stationary target under canonical ad-rss-lib constants.

description: 30 + 1.75 + 33.5²/8 − 0 = 31.75 + 140.28125 = 172.03125 m. Note this exceeds our earlier NHTSA/strict-RSS S7 (167.625 m) precisely because ad-rss-lib uses a_max_accel = 3.5 vs. our strict default of 3.0.

scenario_source.notes: Matched-speed highway following at 108 km/h — the canonical ad-rss-lib lead-car-braking probe.
Urban-speed matched pair, 36 km/h both vehicles. Validates the formula in a regime where term4 (front brake) is material.
Ego closing on slower lead (5 m/s positive differential). Ensures the formula behaves cleanly with a non-matched positive closing rate.

Euro NCAP CCRs 50 km/h test geometry evaluated under ad-rss-lib constants rather than Shalev-Shwartz defaults. Demonstrates our crate produces library-parity distances regardless of which published constant-set is selected.

description: v = 50/3.6 ≈ 13.889 m/s. 13.889 + 1.75 + 17.389²/8 ≈ 53.436 m. (Compare to strict-RSS Euro NCAP CCRs fixture: 51.043 m — the difference is purely the 3.5 vs. 3.0 a_max_accel constant.)

scenario_source.notes: Ego moving slower than lead — no safe-distance requirement because front pulls away. Formula output is negative before clamp; ad-rss-lib and MGAI-auto both clamp to 0.
